design_decision.chosen: A - deny-list: enumerate write mechanisms, resolve their targets, deny the targets outside scope

measured_evidence.corpus: 26 session transcripts, 2274 Bash calls, 2070 unique commands - every Bash command this fleet has ever run. Measured by the architect, not assumed.
measured_evidence.naive_write_verb_hit_rate: 924 of 2070 = 45% of real fleet commands contain a write-shaped token

design_decision.why_not_B: B needs an allow-list of provably read-only commands. Every test runner a builder uses (pytest, node test.js, npm run build) writes files nobody can prove otherwise, to paths (dist/, .pytest_cache/, node_modules/) that will never appear in an approved plan. Under B those are denied. 45% of the real corpus is already write-shaped under a NAIVE matcher; under B the denial rate approaches 100% minus a hand-list. A guard that denies pytest is disabled within a day, and a disabled guard closes nothing. B also does not buy what it claims: it fails closed against a builder that is not trying to evade, and fails anyway against one that is - a base64 payload in python -c, or a script written to an approved file and then executed, defeats any PreToolUse string parser. The population here is cooperative: gap 13 exists BECAUSE s1-whoop voluntarily avoided Bash writes and reported the hole itself. A deny-list catches the cooperative-but-convenient builder, which is 100 percent of the observed population.
design_decision.fail_direction: A fails OPEN on the unknown, stated in words rather than implied. Where the parser sees a write shape but cannot resolve a target (the 126 variable/substitution redirects), the guard ALLOWS and emits a warning naming the unresolved write. That closes the trace half of gap 13 even where it cannot close the denial half - the gap 13 complaint is no denial, no record, no trace, and this leaves a record.

false_positive_budget.hard_and_gating: 0 denials for any command containing no write signature - guaranteed structurally by a pre-filter that runs before any disk I/O. 0 denials across a fixture of at least 30 real read-only builder commands lifted from the corpus: git status, git log, git diff, git checkout -b, git add, git worktree, grep, ls, wc, python -m pytest, node test.js.
false_positive_budget.measured_and_reported: the unresolvable-write-shape rate over all 2070 unique corpus commands. Target 3 percent or lower (62 or fewer). Reported as a number in gate_results; if the builder cannot reach it, it reports the real number rather than fudging it, and the reviewer decides.
false_positive_budget.explicitly_accepted_as_allows: a write to /dev/null, to /tmp, to the state.json of the open run, or to any path inside the approved set. The guard must resolve targets well enough to judge the 790 literal-path redirects on their target rather than on their shape.

plan.intent: Build the write-target classifier as a STANDALONE, IMPORTABLE module that guard-builder-scope.py does not yet import, plus its self-test and a corpus measurement tool. classify(command) returns (resolved_targets, unresolved_write_shape). Covers all 10 evidenced mechanisms - redirect, append, heredoc-to-file, tee, install, dd, truncate, mv, cp, git checkout/restore/apply - plus sed -i, rm, touch, mkdir, and interpreter bodies (python/node/perl with -c or -e, and python - fed by a heredoc) which are INSPECTED for a write signature (open with w/a/x mode, write_text, writeFileSync, json.dump, shutil.copy/move/rmtree, os.remove/rename/makedirs) rather than flagged wholesale. Resolves VAR=value assignments appearing earlier in the same command string before giving up on a target. Owns NO path matching of its own: it returns paths and nothing else, and no opinion about scope lives in this file.

architect.rationale: SHAPE IS FORCED, and not by the repo check. graph_agents IS a git repo (master, clean, fa60664), so a diamond is not excluded on isolation grounds - but feature-graph step 0.5 check 2 fires. The change makes prose FALSE in two files on the forcing list: .claude/agents/builder.md (step 1: a PreToolUse hook denies any Write/Edit outside it) and .claude/skills/feature-graph/SKILL.md (step 5 line 125: denies a Write/Edit from any builder). Both must change or a builder is actively taught that Bash is unwatched. That is single-loop, mandatory, regardless of slice count. GRAPH.md section 5 line 353 says the same thing and must change too, though GRAPH.md is not itself on the forcing list. The orchestrator must tell the user to start a fresh session before the next fleet run. || THE LIVE-HOOK HAZARD ARGUES FOR SEQUENCE INDEPENDENTLY, and it shapes the slicing rather than just the shape. guard-builder-scope.py is registered, live in this session, fails closed, and re-reads state.json on every call with no caching. A builder editing it is editing the thing policing its own writes, and a half-written hook does not degrade to unguarded - it degrades to every builder write denied, with the fix itself denied. So: YES, a slice must avoid touching the live hook directly, and s1 is built so that it does not. The classifier is born as its own file that nothing imports; all the hard, iterative, likely-to-be-wrong work happens while the live hook stays byte-identical and valid. Only s2 touches it, and by then s2 is a thin import-plus-call against a tested contract - the smallest possible invalid window. Two further consequences, both written into the s2 intent: the import must sit inside the try in main(), and the s2 builder should prefer a whole-file Write over a sequence of Edits so the invalid window is one instant rather than several. || ONE HOOK, NOT TWO. The matcher extends to Write|Edit|Bash on the existing guard rather than adding a second hook beside guard-commit-trailers.py. A second file would have to either duplicate approved_paths / _match / worktree_context - the exact drift bug this guard has been fixed for TWICE, and the reason _match() was consolidated into one function - or import them from a hyphenated filename that is not importable without importlib gymnastics. One hook also means one plan-scope deny message and one place a builder learns the rule. The cost is real and is paid for in s2: the guard now runs on every Bash call, so a write-signature pre-filter runs before open_run() and the 55 percent of commands with no write shape touch no disk at all. || SLICES ARE DISJOINT BY FILE even though they are sequential, so each reviewer sees a clean diff and no slice can be blamed for an edit belonging to another. s1 is three new files, s2 is the hook plus its test plus settings.json, s3 is four prose files. No file appears in two slices. || ALL THREE ARE risk high, with a stated reason each rather than an assertion. None of them is small. The s1 test cannot see whether the mechanism list is complete, and its measurement tool reads real transcripts containing owner paths. s2 can lock the session out. The only mechanical check s3 has is grep, against a document whose job is to not overclaim - and the human named overclaiming as the specifically worse outcome, so s3 earns the tag on that alone.
